title: Whole Foods, L.L. Bean and 122 Toll townhomes fill out the District at Black Rock
summary: The mixed-use project rising on the old Quest Diagnostics campus at 1201 S. Collegeville Road is 89 percent pre-leased as construction starts, with Whole Foods, L.L. Bean and Barnes & Noble anchoring more than 148,000 square feet of retail alongside J. Crew, Sephora and Shake Shack. Toll Brothers bought an adjacent 7.3 acres for 122 townhomes, and the center is slated to finish in late 2027.
loc: 1201 S. Collegeville Road, Upper Providence Township

title: Phoenixville Hospital lost $10 million while parent Tower Health turned its first profit
summary: Audited results for the year ended June 30 show Tower Health earning an $8.5 million operating profit on $2.07 billion in revenue, its first since forming in 2017, but Phoenixville Hospital, its last acute-care hospital in Chester County, lost $10 million. Reading Hospital carried the system while Pottstown Hospital and the physician group posted deeper losses.

title: Borough orders gasoline cleanup under the Rita's lot on Nutt Road
summary: Leaking underground tanks from the property's gas station days left gasoline in the groundwater at 472 and 478 Nutt Road, now home to Rita's Water Ice. The borough has told owner Three Six Properties to file a remedial investigation report and cleanup plan with the state DEP; work dates have not been set.

title: Spring City Road bridge replacement now aims for summer 2027
summary: Chester County says the 1958 single-span bridge over Stony Run in East Pikeland, under construction since March, should reopen sometime in summer 2027. Spring City Road stays closed between Township Line Road and Wall Street, with a six-mile detour in place until then.
loc: Spring City Road at Stony Run, East Pikeland Township

title: Private club proposed for residential block of Gay Street goes to zoning board Nov. 18
summary: The 1978 Phoenix Foundation is asking the Zoning Hearing Board for a special exception to run a private club and community center, plus a variance for office use, at 315 Gay St. in the Residential Infill District. The hearing is 7 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18, at Borough Hall, and the application can be inspected there.

title: Valley Forge park draws nearly 800,000 summer visitors in record tourism year
summary: At its Oct. 29 annual luncheon, the Valley Forge Tourism & Convention Board reported record summer visitation at Valley Forge National Historical Park during its 50th year as a national park. Visitor spending in Montgomery County reached $1.8 billion in 2025, and hotels are on pace for about $300 million in room revenue this year.
loc: Valley Forge National Historical Park, Valley Forge

title: Rail authority spends $654,000 to model passenger trains through Phoenixville
summary: The Schuylkill River Passenger Rail Authority voted Oct. 26 to put two state grants toward Amtrak-led simulations of the Reading-Pottstown-Phoenixville-Philadelphia line, coordinated with Norfolk Southern and SEPTA, rather than wait on federal sign-off for phase two. The modeling will show whether the tracks can carry passenger trains alongside freight and what upgrades would cost; the authority still says service could start as early as 2030.

title: Phoenixville schools steer families to food help during SNAP disruption
summary: The Phoenixville Area School District issued a food-security notice pointing affected households to free school breakfast, meal-aid applications, the PACS pantry and Ann's Heart. Its Phoenixville Phamily Fund with Ann's Heart can also cover emergency food and shelter needs.

title: Route 23 safety rebuild through Phoenixville wraps up
summary: PennDOT says major construction is finished on its $2.5 million project covering 11 signalized intersections on Nutt Road, Schuylkill Road and Valley Forge Road in the borough, East Pikeland and Schuylkill Township. The work added a left-turn lane at Township Line Road and reconfigured the Nutt Road and Bridge Street intersection; brief single-lane closures continue for finishing touches.

title: Chicken Salad Chick sets Nov. 18 opening at Providence Town Center
summary: The Southern fast-casual chain's first Philadelphia-area restaurant takes the former Z!Eats space and will seat 55, with free chicken salad for a year promised to the first 100 guests. The local franchise group plans six locations across Montgomery and Chester counties.
loc: 500 Broad St., Providence Town Center, Collegeville
